channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Federal cyber teams boarded two US-bound energy tankers at sea after both ships’ networks were found compromised
item.description: The Coast Guard and FBI confirmed on 16 September that joint offshore security boardings took place in the Gulf of Mexico on 21 and 24 August, after indications that the networks of two foreign-flagged commercial tankers bound for US ports had been compromised. Teams of Coast Guard law enforcement officers, Cyber Protection Team members, a vessel inspector and FBI Cyber Action Team operators went aboard each ship to establish the integrity of both the operational and the information technology systems. One of the vessels has now been named: South Korean manager HMM Ocean Service confirmed it was the VL Prosperity, reported to have lost communications for more than thirty hours while sailing from Egypt toward the United States. Investigators are weighing whether Iran, or an opportunist riding the same conflict, was responsible. The agencies report no operational disruption, no loss of vessel stability and no environmental impact. - US Coast Guard and FBI joint statement, reported by CyberScoop; vessel identification confirmed by ship manager HMM Ocean Service to CBS News; cargo and Gibraltar detail from ABC News - Boardings 21 and 24 Aug 2026; agencies’ joint statement 16 Sep 2026; vessel named in follow-up reporting — verified 17 Sep 2026, 12:20 AM ET

item.title: [Critical] A Sandworm-linked APT and a Qilin ransomware operator are exploiting Cisco firewall management: a critical auth bypass, exploited since August
item.category: Incident — confirmed exploitation of firewall management; an APT overlapping Sandworm tooling and a Qilin ransomware operator
item.description: Cisco and CISA confirmed on 9 September that CVE-2026-20079 — a critical authentication bypass in Secure Firewall Management Center, patched back in March — has been exploited since August. Crafted HTTP requests reach a process created at boot and hand an unauthenticated attacker root on the appliance that configures your firewalls. Cisco Talos tracks three activity clusters across this flaw and a second FMC bug, CVE-2026-20316: one harvesting credentials with a web shell; an APT whose tooling overlaps with Sandworm, delivering a Cyclops Blink variant; and a ransomware operator that came in through CVE-2026-20316 and ultimately deployed Qilin. The KEV remediation deadline of 12 September has now passed. For OT defenders the significance is not the firewall — it is the management plane above it. Whoever holds FMC holds the rule set separating enterprise from plant, and can rewrite it without touching a single controller. - CVE-2026-20079 - Patched Mar 2026; exploitation began Aug 2026; Cisco and Talos disclosure and KEV addition 9 Sep 2026; reported 10 Sep 2026, 6:06 AM ET; KEV remediation deadline 12 Sep 2026, now passed — re-verified 15 Sep 2026, 4:00 PM ET

item.title: [High] An industrial automation vendor lost its SCADA/HMI source code — to a public proof-of-concept weaponised within days
item.category: Incident — n-day exploitation campaign; industrial automation, energy, government and election-adjacent targets in five countries
item.description: Acronis Threat Research Unit published findings on 13 September describing a PRC-linked, Chinese-speaking actor it tracks as Red Heron, which turned a public proof-of-concept for a critical Gitea remote code execution flaw (CVE-2026-60004) into an automated mass-exploitation campaign within days of the code appearing. The operators scanned 1,386 internet-facing Gitea instances across seven countries and kept a separate list of 477 Taiwan-based systems, classified by target type: defence, energy, aerospace, telecommunications, government, research and election or voting systems. Acronis confirmed compromises at eleven organisations in Canada, the United States, Taiwan, Argentina and Sri Lanka; The Hacker News counts 13 organisations in six countries, so read the victim count as at least eleven. The heaviest loss was a Taiwanese industrial automation company, from which the operators pulled hundreds of repositories including a SCADA/HMI product, surveillance and monitoring software, IoT platform integrations and a network sniffer. - CVE-2026-60004 - Acronis TRU report 13 Sep 2026; Industrial Cyber report 15 Sep 2026, 5:11 AM ET; KEV status corrected 16 Sep 2026

item.title: [High] The water campaign was not the whole campaign — telecoms and energy control systems are now being probed, and there is a $10 million bounty on the man said to run it
item.category: Targeting — Iran-linked campaign widens beyond water into telecommunications and energy; attempts reported, no confirmed OT impact
item.description: Two developments this week moved the summer’s dominant OT story past the water sector. NBC News reported on 2 September, citing four people with access to government and industry threat information, that Iran-linked operators have spent recent weeks probing internet-facing automated control systems at telecommunications and energy providers as well as water utilities — and that those attempts have so far been unsuccessful. A day later the State Department’s Rewards for Justice programme posted a reward of up to $10 million for information identifying or locating Amir Yaryab, named as head of the cyber operations division of the IRGC Cyber-Electronic Command and accused of directing groups including the CyberAv3ngers persona against US critical infrastructure. Separately, a Telegram channel presenting itself as a voice for Iranian cyber operations has threatened action against US energy, water and telecommunications, without evidence of any successful operation. The signal for defenders is the change of aim, not a new capability: the same tradecraft that found exposed water PLCs in July is now being pointed at neighbouring sectors that run the same internet-facing gear. - NBC News reporting on expanded targeting and the State Department Rewards for Justice announcement, as carried by The Record — water-campaign scale from CISA and SecurityWeek - NBC report 2 Sep 2026; $10 million reward announced 3 Sep 2026 — verified 15 Sep 2026, 10:49 AM ET

item.title: [Critical] A small UK generating station ran manually for four days after an Iran-linked cyberattack
item.category: Incident — Confirmed OT disruption, power generation (UK)
item.description: A small British power generating station was taken offline for four days by a cyberattack, with staff forced to restore operations manually. The Telegraph broke the story on 22 August; the UK government confirmed that a small-scale generator had been affected while stating there was at no point a risk to the national energy system, and the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero has since contacted power companies about the risk. UK assessments reported by the Telegraph point to hackers affiliated with the Iranian regime, likely the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps. The site’s size is the uncomfortable part rather than a reassurance: distributed generation, embedded generators and behind-the-meter assets sit below most reporting thresholds, are often remotely operated by a third party, and are numerous enough that an attack that works once is repeatable. - SecurityWeek and CNBC, both citing the originating Telegraph report and the UK government statement - Incident occurred July 2026; reported 22–23 Aug 2026; government response reported 24 Aug 2026 — re-verified 15 Sep 2026, 10:49 AM ET

item.title: [Medium] A municipal utility lost its whole back office and kept the lights on — the separation held, and it is worth reading why
item.category: Incident — confirmed IT encryption at a multi-utility; electricity, water and district heating supply unaffected (Germany)
item.description: Stadtwerke Landsberg am Lech, the Bavarian municipal utility that supplies electricity, water, wastewater, district heating and fibre to a town of roughly 30,000, disclosed a criminal cyberattack that encrypted its central IT systems on 1 September 2026. File servers, the ERP database and administrative server clusters were either encrypted or pre-emptively shut down; corporate email and VoIP telephony were cut from external networks, leaving customers unable to reach the utility by phone or email for days. The utility stated that the systems controlling electricity, water and heat supply were not affected and continued to run normally. It disconnected the affected environment from the internet, stood up a crisis team and brought in external responders; by 7 September enough administrative capability was restored to resume customer service and contract processing. No group has claimed the attack and the utility has not said whether an extortion demand was made. It cannot yet rule out theft of customer names, addresses, contact details and bank data, and a GDPR data-subject notice posted on 7 September warns customers that their data may have been exposed. - Stadtwerke Landsberg statements, reported by The Record (Recorded Future News) and T&D World - Attack disclosed 1 Sep 2026; administrative systems substantially restored 7 Sep 2026; reported 11 Sep 2026 — verified 16 Sep 2026, 4:30 AM ET

item.title: [Medium] Four ways to knock a Siemens edge gateway off the PROFINET segment — and blind SCADA while you do it
item.category: Nozomi Networks Labs research — PROFINET DCP memory corruption in a Siemens OT/IT edge gateway
item.description: Nozomi Networks Labs published research on 15 September detailing four memory-corruption flaws in the PROFINET Discovery and basic Configuration Protocol implementation on the Siemens SCALANCE LPE9403 industrial PC, found using emulation-driven snapshot fuzzing with the Unicorn CPU emulator and AFL++. The flaws are tracked as CVE-2025-40575 through CVE-2025-40578 — an uninitialised-value issue, a NULL pointer dereference and two out-of-bounds reads — each carrying a CVSS 4.0 score of 5.3, and affect firmware up to V4.0 HF0. The DCP daemon runs as root, requires no authentication and is bound to all three device interfaces, so an attacker already on the same Layer 2 segment can crash it with crafted Ethernet frames. Siemens has shipped fixed firmware. - CVE-2025-40575 - Published 15 Sep 2026, 5:15 AM ET

item.title: [Info] Six agencies publish the 17 ways attackers take Active Directory — which is how most of them reach a control network
item.category: Guidance — six-nation technical publication on Active Directory attack techniques; directly relevant to the IT-to-OT pivot
item.description: On 15 September 2026, CISA, the NSA, Australia’s ASD, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, New Zealand’s NCSC and the UK’s NCSC jointly published guidance describing seventeen techniques the agencies observe being used against Microsoft Active Directory, with detection and mitigation advice for each. It spans Active Directory Domain Services, Certificate Services and Federation Services, and covers credential theft, Kerberoasting and AS-REP roasting, Kerberos ticket forgery, directory-replication abuse, certificate-template abuse, privilege escalation, lateral movement, persistence and hybrid-identity compromise. This is an enterprise-identity publication rather than an ICS one, which is precisely why it belongs here: in the great majority of documented OT intrusions the adversary does not exploit a controller to get in — they take the domain first, then walk into engineering workstations, historians, HMIs and jump hosts holding valid credentials. Several of the seventeen work equally well against an OT domain that trusts, or is trusted by, the corporate one. - CISA, NSA, ASD, CCCS, NCSC-NZ and NCSC-UK joint guidance - Published 15 Sep 2026 — verified 16 Sep 2026, 4:30 AM ET

item.title: [Critical] The box that decides which VLAN a device lands in can now be taken by an unauthenticated HTTP request — and it is already being taken
item.category: Cisco Identity Services Engine and ISE-PIC — CVE-2026-76460, CVSS 10.0, unauthenticated root, exploited in the wild; KEV-listed the same day
item.description: Cisco published advisory cisco-sa-ISE-ABP-VNSW7Tn5 at 4:00 PM GMT today: CVE-2026-76460 is a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass in an Identity Services Engine API endpoint, and the PSIRT says it is aware of active exploitation. A crafted request to the endpoint bypasses the web management interface entirely; Cisco warns that successful exploitation can yield command execution as root. Every ISE and ISE-PIC release before the fixed patch level is affected regardless of configuration, and there is no workaround — only an infrastructure ACL in front of the management plane. CISA added it to KEV within hours. For OT this is the segmentation story, not an IT one: ISE is what many plants rely on to decide which device is allowed onto the control VLAN, and it holds the RADIUS and TACACS+ secrets for the switches enforcing that decision. - CVE-2026-76460 - Cisco disclosure 16 Sep 2026, 16:00 GMT; KEV addition 16 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] The hypervisor under your SCADA estate is now a ransomware target — and CISA said so at the weekend
item.category: Broadcom VMware vCenter Server — CVE-2026-59310, CVSS 9.8, exploited since August and now flagged by CISA as used in ransomware campaigns
item.description: CISA updated its KEV entry for CVE-2026-59310 over the weekend of 13–14 September to record that ransomware operators have joined the attacks on it. The flaw is a critical directory-traversal weakness in the vCenter Syslog service, patched by Broadcom on 29 July, which lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access run arbitrary code on the management server. DFIR firm QUIRSO reported over 361 compromised IP addresses in 47 countries two weeks after the fix, from an actor deploying a reverse-SSH tool for persistence; CISA added the CVE to KEV on 18 August with a three-day federal deadline. Shadowserver still sees more than 450 vCenter servers exposed to the internet. For OT this is not an IT story: the historian, HMI and engineering virtual machines on the other side of that hypervisor are the ones that stop. - CVE-2026-59310 - Patched 29 Jul 2026; KEV addition 18 Aug 2026; ransomware flag added to KEV entry 13–14 Sep 2026; reported 15 Sep 2026, 8:16 AM ET

item.title: [Critical] An email is now a root shell: Cisco’s mail gateway is being exploited as a zero-day, and it takes no clicks at all
item.category: Cisco Secure Email Gateway (AsyncOS) — CVE-2026-76461, CVSS 9.8, exploited as a zero-day; KEV-listed 14 Sep, federal deadline 17 Sep
item.description: Cisco told customers on Monday that CVE-2026-76461, a CVSS 9.8 flaw in the email-parsing logic of AsyncOS, has been exploited in the wild as a zero-day. A remote, unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted message containing malicious SQL statements; insufficient validation in the parser executes them, ending in arbitrary operating-system commands as root on the appliance. No credentials, no user interaction, no one has to open anything. Both physical and virtual Secure Email Gateways are affected in any configuration; Secure Email and Web Manager and Secure Web Appliance are not. CISA added it to KEV the same day with a 17 September federal deadline. For OT programmes the uncomfortable part is second-order: this is the second Cisco appliance in a week under confirmed attack, and both sit upstream of the enterprise identity your plant network still trusts. - CVE-2026-76461 - Cisco disclosure and KEV addition 14 Sep 2026; reported 15 Sep 2026, 1:18 AM ET; KEV remediation deadline 17 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] The VPN box your integrators dial in through can be walked past without a password — and has been since 3 September
item.category: Citrix NetScaler ADC & NetScaler Gateway — CVE-2026-19490, CVSS 9.3, authentication bypass exploited in the wild; KEV-listed, federal deadline passed 12 Sep
item.description: CISA warned on 9 September that CVE-2026-19490 is being exploited, and added it to the KEV catalogue with a three-day federal remediation clock under BOD 26-04. The flaw is an authentication bypass using an alternate path (CWE-288) rated CVSS 9.3, and it reaches every NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway appliance configured as a Gateway — SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN or RDP Proxy — or as an AAA virtual server. A remote attacker with no credentials bypasses the login protections and reaches functionality that should require a valid account. Citrix patched it on 19 August; Rapid7 said at the time that exploitation was likely to follow quickly. It did. A public exploit appeared on GitHub on 2 September and telemetry shows attacks from 3 September onward. For OT programmes this is the familiar shape: the appliance that terminates vendor and integrator remote sessions into the plant is now a pre-authentication foothold, and RDP Proxy and ICA Proxy are exactly the modes used to hand an OEM a jump-host session. - CVE-2026-19490 - Patched 19 Aug 2026; exploitation observed from 3 Sep 2026; KEV addition 9 Sep 2026; reported 10 Sep 2026, 8:20 AM ET — verified 16 Sep 2026

item.title: [Critical] The router at the unmanned site can be taken over the SSH port without a password — and it was being taken a day before the fix shipped
item.category: CERT Polska / MikroTik — RouterOS SSH authentication bypass chain “MikroTrick”; CVSS 9.2; exploited in the wild since 2 Sep
item.description: CERT Polska coordinated the disclosure of six RouterOS flaws and has named the two that chain together “MikroTrick”: CVE-2026-67276, an SSH authentication bypass, and CVE-2026-86060, a crafted-username flaw that hands over full administrative privileges — both rated CVSS 9.2. Together they give an unauthenticated attacker complete control of any RouterOS device whose SSH service is reachable. CERT Polska reports that attacks, including creation of an account named “ops”, began on 2 September from a single source address — a day before MikroTik published the patched builds on 3 September. Researchers have also flagged an SSH user named “-2” as an indicator on compromised devices. This matters in OT because MikroTik gear is cheap, ubiquitous and quietly load-bearing: it terminates cellular and radio backhaul at remote pump stations, wellpads, substations and telemetry sites, and it is frequently installed by an integrator, never inventoried by the plant, and never patched. - CVE-2026-67276 - Published 5 Sep 2026; exploitation confirmed from 2 Sep 2026 — verified 17 Sep 2026, 12:20 AM ET

item.title: [Critical] One firmware, three nameplates: unauthenticated admin access and root-level file upload in IO-Link masters from three vendors
item.category: CERT@VDE VDE-2026-014, -027 and -028 — shared IO-Link master firmware; CVSS 9.8 across Phoenix Contact, Pepperl+Fuchs and Carlo Gavazzi
item.description: CERT@VDE published three coordinated advisories on 16 September for IO-Link master devices built on a common firmware base below version 1.7.4: Phoenix Contact IOL MA8 EIP DI8 and IOL MA8 PN DI8 (VDE-2026-027, 19 CVEs), the Pepperl+Fuchs ICE2 and ICE3 families (VDE-2026-014, 24 CVEs) and Carlo Gavazzi YL212 and YN115 models (VDE-2026-028, 20 CVEs). The two worst are rated CVSS 9.8: CVE-2026-27546, an unauthenticated authentication bypass to administrator, and CVE-2026-27565, an unauthenticated upload of a malicious IODD device-description file that runs a shell script as root. Many further command-injection flaws score 8.8, and others leak password hashes and SSH private keys. Phoenix Contact’s advisory credits Nozomi Networks with the research. IO-Link masters sit at the very bottom of the plant network, between field sensors and actuators and the controller, and the same defect arriving under three brands is a reminder that the name on the housing does not tell you whose firmware is inside. - CVE-2026-27546 - Published 16 Sep 2026 — verified 16 Sep 2026, 7:55 AM ET

item.title: [Critical] A CVSS 9.2 in the authentication of a safety-rated PLC — and the fix is an application-level change, not a firmware drop
item.category: Schneider Electric September Patch Tuesday — Modicon M580 and M580 Safety controllers; CVE-2026-3869, CVSS 9.2
item.description: Schneider Electric’s September advisories include CVE-2026-3869, an incorrect implementation of the authentication algorithm (CWE-303) in Modicon M580 and Modicon M580 Safety controllers, rated CVSS 9.2. The condition applies where the controller is running an application project built at an application level below 4.00, or below 4.20 for the Safety range, and can lead to loss of confidentiality, integrity and availability of the PLC. Schneider published four new advisories and updated four others in the same batch, including high-severity issues in the PowerLogic T300 (formerly Easergy T300) RTU and EcoStruxure IT Data Center Expert, and a medium-severity flaw in SCADAPack x70. The M580 is a mainstream process and safety controller across water, power, oil and gas and manufacturing, which is what lifts this above the usual advisory traffic — and the remediation path runs through the engineering application, so it needs a change window and a revalidation, not an overnight patch. - CVE-2026-3869 - Published 8 Sep 2026 — verified 17 Sep 2026, 12:20 AM ET

item.title: [High] CISA’s 15 September batch puts a protection relay, a ship-fleet system and a SCADA manager on the same list
item.category: ICSA-26-258-01 to -08 — CISA’s 15 September batch; Siemens Reyrolle 7SR5 and mySCADA myPRO at CVSS 9.8
item.description: CISA released eight ICS advisories on 15 September, plus two updates. The heaviest for grid operators is ICSA-26-258-05, CISA’s republication of Siemens SSA-142885 (first issued 8 September) for the Reyrolle 7SR5 protection relay: 14 CVEs in versions before V2.70, led by CVE-2026-62645, missing authentication for a critical function at CVSS 9.8, and CVE-2026-62650, an authentication bypass at 8.8. ICSA-26-258-03 covers mySCADA myPRO Manager 2.1 and earlier, where CVE-2026-73807 (missing authorisation, 9.8) and CVE-2026-82567 could expose privileged management functions or send arbitrary SMS through a connected GSM modem; version 2.2 fixes both. ICSA-26-258-02 covers Wärtsilä FOS-Onboard 5.07.0923.01, where two hard-coded cryptographic keys (CVE-2026-78225 at 9.0 and CVE-2026-81855 at 9.1) could allow unauthorised update delivery, code execution or credential extraction — Wärtsilä says they are not exploitable when the product is installed as recommended. The rest of the batch: Digital Watchdog VMAX recorders with hard-coded credentials (9.6), CareCam CM2507 cameras with no fix because the vendor did not respond to CISA, Schneider Electric SCADAPack x70 RTUs (6.5), Siemens Mendix SAML (8.7) and Siemens Teamcenter (6.1). CISA also updated its Siemens OpenSSL (ICSA-26-174-03) and SICAM 8 (ICSA-26-197-05) advisories. - CVE-2026-62645 - Published 15 Sep 2026 — verified 16 Sep 2026, 7:55 AM ET

item.title: [High] A hard-coded key and MD5 hashes inside pipeline integrity monitoring — read access to the project files is enough
item.category: ICSA-26-253-01 — AVEVA Pipeline Integrity Monitor (PIMBoards); CVE-2026-81821 at CVSS 8.3, plus MD5 password hashing
item.description: AVEVA published an advisory, republished by CISA as ICSA-26-253-01, covering four flaws in the PIMBoards component of Pipeline Integrity Monitor. Two matter most. CVE-2026-81821, rated CVSS 8.3, is a hard-coded cryptographic key: anyone who can read the affected project files can decrypt the sensitive information inside them, with no privileged access to the application required. The second is the use of MD5 to hash passwords, which puts administrative credentials within reach of anyone who obtains the stored hashes. All versions prior to the 2025 SP1 P2 release are affected. Pipeline Integrity Monitor is the application operators use to watch for leaks, corrosion and pressure anomalies across a pipeline network, so its project files describe segment layout, instrumentation and alarm thresholds — reconnaissance material for anyone planning to interfere with the process, and a credential path into the monitoring application itself. - CVE-2026-81821 - Published 10 Sep 2026 — verified 16 Sep 2026, 3:25 PM ET

item.title: [Medium] The clock has started: anyone selling a connected product into the EU now owes a 24-hour warning on exploited vulnerabilities
item.category: EU Cyber Resilience Act — Reporting obligations IN FORCE since 11 Sep 2026
item.description: The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered its reporting phase on 11 September 2026. As of yesterday, manufacturers of products with digital elements must report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe security incidents affecting their products, with an early warning inside 24 hours and a fuller notification inside 72 hours. The scope reaches far past consumer IoT: PLCs, RTUs, drives, gateways, HMIs, protocol converters and the engineering software around them are products with digital elements, and the obligation follows the manufacturer regardless of where the affected device is installed. Legal analysts advise naming an owner now and building the assessment, escalation and customer-communication path in advance, coordinating it with existing NIS2 and GDPR duties rather than standing up a third parallel process. - Industrial Cyber report of 11 Sep 2026 on the reporting rules taking effect, with Freshfields analysis via Lexology - Analysis published 1 Sep 2026; reporting obligations in force from 11 Sep 2026; take-effect reporting 11 Sep 2026 — verified 15 Sep 2026, 10:49 AM ET

item.title: [Info] Comments close on 9 October: the government is asking the industry how to decide which grid equipment is too foreign to install
item.category: Regulation — DOE CESER request for information implementing Executive Order 14421; US bulk-power system supply chain
item.description: Executive Order 14421 declares a national emergency over the security of the US bulk-power system and prohibits the acquisition, importation, transfer or installation of foreign-produced bulk-power electric equipment that is connected to a covered foreign entity and presents a defined national security risk. On 9 September 2026 the Department of Energy’s Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security and Emergency Response issued a request for information seeking public comment on how to implement it, covering which equipment and entities should be in scope, supply chain risk management practices, what happens to equipment already installed, and the domestic manufacturing and economic consequences. DOE held a public webinar on 16 September; comments are due on or about 9 October 2026, with final implementing rules expected on or about 24 December 2026 and recommendations for Federal Acquisition Regulation revisions around 22 February 2027. - DOE CESER request for information under Executive Order 14421 — summarised by Holland & Knight - RFI issued 9 Sep 2026; comments due on or about 9 Oct 2026 — verified 17 Sep 2026, 12:20 AM ET

item.title: [Info] FERC signs off on CIP-014-4 — a tighter, more consistent test for which substations count as critical
item.category: Regulation — FERC approves a revised NERC reliability standard; North American bulk-power system
item.description: FERC issued an order on 10 September 2026 approving NERC Reliability Standard CIP-014-4, published in the Federal Register on 15 September. CIP-014 is the physical security standard for the bulk-power system, and this revision targets the part registered entities have found most contestable: how transmission stations, transmission substations and primary control centres are identified and assessed as critical to reliable operation. The revision pushes toward a more consistent, repeatable identification methodology across entities rather than adding a new control set. It is a physical-security standard, but OT security staff should not file it under someone else’s programme — the risk assessment that decides a station is critical is the same assessment that should be driving cyber scoping for the relays, RTUs, protection schemes and communications at that station, and at many utilities the two exercises are still run separately, years apart, on different criteria. - Federal Register — FERC order approving NERC Reliability Standard CIP-014-4 - Order issued 10 Sep 2026; published in the Federal Register 15 Sep 2026 — verified 16 Sep 2026, 4:30 AM ET
